validity.researcher_notes: GEM's own gem.wiki page for this pipeline carries exactly one citation: 'World Energy Atlas, Petroleum Economist, 2001' — a print atlas with no URL, unverifiable and (per standing rules) not citable regardless. wiki_citations.json independently confirms zero harvestable citations for this row. So the sheet has never had an independently checkable source for this entity at all. I then tried to independently confirm the pipeline via the SAME authoritative source that underpins nearly every other pipeline in this 30-row Libya gas roster: OPEC's Annual Statistical Bulletin 2012, Table 4.10 'Gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2011' (p.75; live opec.org copy 301-redirects to the homepage, retrieved instead via the Wayback Machine capture and confirmed with curl+pdftotext, since url_verifier's substring screen cannot read binary PDF byte streams — same documented false-negative as sibling row P1869). That single OPEC table lists 21 named Libyan gas pipelines and its length/diameter/capacity figures match — essentially exactly, after mi->km and 1,000 scm/yr->bcm/y conversion — 21 of the ~30 pipelines on this project's in-scope roster: Wafa/Mellitah=P0484, Bahr Assalam/Mellitah=P1855/P6713, Mellitah/Gela=P0439 (Greenstream), Intesar/Brega=P1856 (207mi=333km, 42in, 42,480,884 th.scm/yr=42.48 bcm/y — exact match to P1856's cap=42.48), 103D/103A=P1857, Bu-Attifel/Intesar=P1858/P6714, Bouri/Bahr Assalam=P1859/P6709, Waha/Nasser=P1860, Faregh/Intesar=P1861, Brega/Benghazi=P1862, Brega/Khoms=P1863, Khoms/Tripoli=P1864, Tripoli/Mellitah=P1865, Nasser/Brega=P1866, Attahaddy/km-91.5=P1867, Km-81.5/Brega=P1868, Raguba/km-110=P1869, Intesar/Sahel=P1870, Sahel/km-81.5=P1871, Km-91.5/Brega=P1872, Jakhira/Intesar=P1873. This is clearly the (or a) primary data backbone GEM drew this roster from. Crucially, THERE IS NO 'Defa' ENTRY ANYWHERE IN THIS TABLE — not under any of the Libya rows in Table 4.10 (gas), and I also checked Table 4.9 'Crude oil pipelines in OPEC Members, 2011' (pp.71-72) in the same document in case Defa's line was misclassified as oil — it is also absent there (that table's Libya section lists Sarir/Tobruk, Messla/Amal, Nasser/Al-Brayqah, Amal/Ras Lanuf, Aseida/Ras Lanuf, etc., but no Defa route of any kind). P0482 is one of only a handful of roster rows (alongside P0483 Libya Coastal [a rollup, expected], P3987, P3988, P6705, P1789) missing from this table, and it is distinctive in that its Diameter and Capacity are BOTH still blank in the mainsheet — unlike every OPEC-sourced row, which has all three of length/diameter/capacity populated from that table. Separately, I confirmed 'Defa' IS a real place-name in Libya's Sirte Basin: two Wikipedia geology articles ('Zelten oil field' and 'Raguba field'), both citing a USGS Sirte Basin Province assessment and an academic paper (Belazi, 'The geology of the Nafoora oil field, Sirte basin, Libya', Journal of Petroleum Geology v.12, 1989), describe Defa as one of the Sirte Basin's 'giant oil fields' in the north-center trend, sometimes styled jointly as 'Defa-Waha field' — so the field itself is not invented. But no source found ties Defa to Brega by a dedicated 299km gas line. The only named 'Defa' pipeline I could find anywhere is on Wikipedia's 'Ras Lanuf' article, which twice describes a 'Defa-Ra's Lanuf' OIL pipeline (~251km) — a different commodity and a different endpoint than GEM records — but that specific claim's own citation is Theodora.com/pipelines, a source this project blocklists as an unreliable tertiary aggregator, and it is NOT corroborated by the OPEC table either, so I cannot treat it as confirmation of anything, only as a hint that if a real 'Defa' pipeline exists in the literature at all, everything else about it (commodity, endpoint) contradicts GEM's P0482 record. Net: I could not independently confirm P0482 as a real, distinct, operating 299km Defa-to-Brega GAS pipeline from any source — GEM's own citation is unverifiable, the authoritative OPEC dataset that backstops almost this entire roster is silent on it (in both its gas AND oil tables), and the one 'Defa' pipeline name that does surface in the wider literature points to a different route and commodity, sourced from a source this project excludes. This meets the sweep's 'GEM-only entity' flag criteria.

validity.recommendation: If Baird's team decides to keep this row pending further research, do not accept 'Brega' as a confirmed endpoint without a better source — verify against the OPEC table's absence and the conflicting Ras Lanuf claim before publishing.
validity.researcher_notes: Beyond the existence doubt above, the specific route recorded (Defa gas field -> Brega, Al Wahat) is itself unconfirmed. The only named 'Defa' pipeline found in any source (Wikipedia's Ras Lanuf article, sourced from the blocklisted Theodora.com) runs Defa -> Ra's Lanuf, not Defa -> Brega, and is described there as carrying oil, not gas. Ras Lanuf and Mersa Brega are two different, well-documented oil/gas port towns roughly 200km apart on the Gulf of Sirte, so this is not a minor naming variance — if there is a real 'Defa' export pipeline, the only lead available says it goes the opposite direction from what GEM records. Also worth noting for context (not a duplicate claim): P1866 'Nasser-Brega Gas Pipeline' (172mi=277km per the same OPEC table) is independently and separately well-corroborated — two different Wikipedia Sirte Basin geology articles describe a real Zelten/Nasser-field-to-Brega gas gathering trunk line — so a Nasser->Brega gas connection is solid; nothing comparable exists for a Defa->Brega connection.

summary: CONCERN (existence): no independent source — including OPEC's ASB2012 Table 4.10, the same authoritative dataset that backstops length/diameter/capacity for 21 of the ~30 roster pipelines — lists a 'Defa-Brega' gas pipeline in either its gas or oil Libya tables; GEM's own wiki citation is an unverifiable, URL-less 2001 print atlas. 'Defa' is a real Sirte Basin oil field (confirmed via independent geology sources) but the only named 'Defa' pipeline found anywhere (Wikipedia, sourced from blocklisted Theodora.com) runs to Ra's Lanuf as an oil line, not to Brega as gas — contradicting GEM's route and commodity.
